doc.title: Dave Bailey and John McNeil Interview, 1959-10-25

title: McNeil in the Gibson brass band and with Kid Clayton
summary: McNeil learned jazz brass band playing from Bailey and Kid Clayton and defends the old-timers' unwritten knowledge.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: What brass bands have you worked with?

Well I've worked with the Gibson brass band and that was the only jazz brass band, you know, that I played with outside of the school band when I was coming up with me. And I was, I got a chance to learn quite a bit, think about jazz more than ever. And because I ran into some of the old timers, you know, in that field, like Dave, and he'd give me a lot of ideas and things that I didn't know and he could hum it and I guess, you know, most of that stuff is played by Ed anyway and you catch the, you really get the knack of it. And I got experience of playing with, another trumpet player of one of the old times that I enjoyed having experience of playing was Kid Clayton too. Clayton, I played a film with him and boy he went back and got some of the old numbers like Panama Rag that I really hadn't heard of, you know, since I was small. And after a couple of courses I already came back to him and I found myself getting right in on it, you know, and it was quite an experience. And I got a chance to play my first film, you know, was with, I played along with Clayton. And that was quite an experience that I had longed for, you know, through the years. Because most of the time I never did go in for brass band music, you know, more or less.
Well he's mighty good, Clayton. Yeah, yeah.
He's a good trumpet player though. You know what I'm talking about.
Do you know your stronger trumpet player than Clayton?

Well, I might be a little stronger but those guys had something to be treasured. I mean, you know, and you can only get it from them by playing along with them and observing it, getting in on it, because they don't write it on paper.
No. Well, he play all that stuff, man. Sure, I better tell them. The band I played years ago, so… These bands come in and you gotta catch with them.
Yeah. A lot of other stuff, man.
Well, here they are. It's all new to the one but I got them covered. Yeah.
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
